newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul stocks close lower, Kia Group shares tumble.
newsitem.headline: Seoul stocks close lower, Kia Group shares tumble.

text.p: Creditor banks decided on Tuesday to bail out South Korea's eighth-largest Kia Group, giving a heavy blow to the Seoul stock market, which had languished in the doldrums on consolidation, brokers said.

The Korea First Bank, Kia's major creditor, said the bail-out committee selected 18 Kia affiliates including all six listed units for rescue. The six Kia shares went limit down before the Korea Stock Exchange suspended trading of Kia affiliates for the afternoon session.
The composite stock index shed 9.40 points, or 1.23 percent, to 755.05, recouping from the day low of 748.47.
